summary: Cupola cabin built 1927 on Hawkeye Point in the Goat Rocks Wilderness, abandoned in 1933 for fog and gone by 1966; the summit has a benchmark, and no cabin remains are described.

facts.status_note: The cabin was gone by 1966. No source describes remains of it on the summit.

access.note: In the Goat Rocks Wilderness and reached on foot. No closure is described in the sources.

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb lists 5 miles one way with 3,300 ft of gain. TrailChick's 2017 loop started at the Berry Patch trailhead near Chambers Lake and climbed a boot path from the Lily Basin trail junction.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Gifford Pinchot National Forest)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1956 newspaper calls the peak 8,000 feet. The register, WillhiteWeb and TrailChick give 7,431 feet, which the record's 2,265 m follows.
The register and firelookout.com say gone by 1966, WillhiteWeb says it likely burned that year, and TrailChick says destroyed in the mid-1960s. All agree it was gone by the mid-1960s.

notes_for_editor: The history (1927 build, 1933 abandonment, gone by 1966) is consistent across four sources. Remains today are not described by any source; the newest first-hand report is TrailChick's July 2017 trip, and no 2020s photo of the summit was read. The Goat Ridge replacement is a separate lookout, with a 1933 L-4 cab that TrailChick says was removed after 1963; it may deserve its own record. The 1956 newspaper's 8,000-foot figure is an approximation, not used.
